newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA STOCKS END LOW DRAGGED DOWN BY BLUE CHIPS.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA STOCKS END LOW DRAGGED DOWN BY BLUE CHIPS.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Thursday after investors sold highly capitalised blue chips, brokers said.

The all-share index closed 1.8 points down at 848.9. Price declines outnumbered gains by 35 to 28. Highly capitalised John Keells Holdings fell five rupees to 365 and National Development Bank dropped five to 275.
"Retailers believe they can get enough money to buy many low-valued shares by selling a few pricey blue chips," said Dimuthu Abeysekera of Allied Phillips Securities.
"That is probably why both John Keells and NDB fell on very small volumes," he added.
Turnover was 85.8 million rupees, led by 170,000 shares of Kelani Tyre, 300,000 Sampath Bank and 80,000 Veytex.
Foreign buying was 6.6 million rupees while selling was 47.3 million.
Foreign and local institutional participation, mainly on the buying side, would remain low ahead of expected public offers by finance and plantations, brokers said.
"Institutional investors are waiting for the NDB offer of 900,000 shares and plantation initial public offers," a broker said.
